title: Claude message queues — four behavior choices

steps.intro: Starting point: YouCoded holds waiting messages and their files, with Edit, Remove, and Interrupt and send now like native chats. This is behavior planning, not a new layout. Offline drafts stay drafts; uncertain delivery is never silently retried. Native queue strip, message box and Context menu are the references.

steps.path: Chat, while the assistant is working
steps.headline: When should Claude read a queued message?
steps.today: Native chats can read your next message after the current batch of tool actions, before deciding what to do next. They need not finish the whole reply first.
steps.problem: Waiting for the whole reply could make Claude queues feel less responsive than native chats, especially during long tasks.
steps.proposal: Choose the target behavior. Matching native timing needs a Claude capability check; we will not quietly substitute different behavior if it cannot be done safely.

options.label: After the current actions
pros: Matches native: your correction can guide the rest of the task.
cons: Needs more verification than simply waiting until Claude is idle.

options.label: After the whole reply
pros: Each message starts a separate response; simpler to follow.
cons: A correction may wait until a long task has already finished.

steps.path: Chat Stop button, with messages already queued
steps.headline: Should Stop pause the waiting messages too?
steps.today: Native Stop interrupts current work but still allows already-submitted user messages to run. Background reports are held separately.
steps.problem: Stopping an unwanted answer could immediately start another one if you have messages waiting.
steps.proposal: Keep the native meaning, or make Claude Stop pause the queue until you continue it. Interrupt and send now would remain an explicit way to run a selected message.

options.label: Stop current work only
pros: Matches native; messages you already sent still get handled.
cons: Stop does not make the conversation stay quiet.

options.label: Stop and pause the queue
pros: Nothing waiting starts until you choose to continue.
cons: Differs from native behavior; adds a continue step.

steps.path: Reopening the app or recovering after a crash
steps.headline: Should waiting messages survive an app restart?
steps.today: The native queue lives in the running session. Its current implementation is not a durable outbox for an app restart.
steps.problem: A queue containing several carefully written messages could disappear when the app exits.
steps.proposal: Save messages the app has not handed to Claude yet, including their attachments, and restore them paused. This is different from guessing whether an uncertain send ran.

options.label: Save and restore paused
pros: Keeps your work without unexpectedly running it when the app reopens.
cons: You must choose to continue the restored queue.

options.label: Keep queues session-only
pros: No stale queue to review when starting again.
cons: Waiting messages do not survive an app exit or crash.

steps.path: Context menu or /clear, with messages waiting
steps.headline: What should Clear do with waiting messages?
steps.today: Clear starts fresh context in the same conversation. The proposed app-owned Claude queue does not exist yet, so its Clear behavior is undecided.
steps.problem: An old queued instruction could run after Clear without the context it relied on.
steps.proposal: Pause dispatch before clearing, then either retain the waiting messages for review or explicitly discard them. Never let an old message slip across Clear accidentally.

options.label: Keep them paused
pros: No lost writing; review what still belongs in the fresh context.
cons: Old messages remain until you remove or continue them.

options.label: Discard with confirmation
pros: Clear means a clean start, including the queue.
cons: An extra confirmation; discarded messages must be rewritten.
